body:
CLAIM: PT/OT/ST furnished by an SNF are the covered type of service for a covered Part A stay.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the services were initiated on August 28, 2009, with treatment diagnoses of muscle weakness and lack of coordination."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §50.3): "must be provided by the SNF or by others under arrangements with the SNF for beneficiaries in either a covered Part A stay"

CLAIM: Therapy appears reasonable and necessary given documented functional decline; SNF residency and certification details are not stated.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "D.E. was referred to PT due to decreased strength and decreased ADLs due to illness."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4.1.1): "The services must be reasonable and necessary for the treatment of the patient’s condition"

CLAIM: A hospital stay of 12 days is reported, which would exceed 3 consecutive days, but direct SNF admission and inpatient status are not documented.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "hospital records concerning the beneficiary’s December 15, 2009, through December 27, 2009, stay at *** *** Hospital"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §100): "as long as some portion of the stay included at least 3 consecutive days of medically necessary inpatient hospital services"

CLAIM: Whether the presumption of coverage applies cannot be determined because the SNF admission date and route are not stated.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "Lastly, the State Medicaid agency contends that the beneficiary’s SNF stay met the criteria for Medicare coverage."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.1): "If the beneficiary is discharged from the hospital to a setting other than the SNF, the presumption of coverage does not apply"

CLAIM: Inpatient coverage requires a practitioner admission order; the case facts do not say whether one existed.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The medical record must contain information that documents the need for an inpatient level of care."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §10.2): "is therefore required for all hospital inpatient cases for hospital inpatient coverage and payment under Part A"

CLAIM: Admission coverage turns on medical judgment, not length of stay; the patient-specific facts are not in the case facts.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "Those cases that appear to be routine, expected discharge within 24 hours"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §10): "Admissions of particular patients are not covered or noncovered solely on the basis of the length of time the patient actually spends in the hospital"

CLAIM: SNF coverage requires a qualifying 3-day hospital stay; the case facts address only briefing deadlines and contain no clinical or stay information.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The appellant filed a timely request for Council review (Form DAB-101), dated August 24, 2009, and received on August 26, 2009."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20): "the individual must have been an inpatient of a hospital for a medically necessary stay of at least three consecutive calendar days"

CLAIM: SNF admission followed a qualifying hospital stay; the policy presumes level of care for direct admission after a 3-day qualifying stay.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "admitted to *** skilled nursing facility (SNF) on January 17, 2006, after a qualifying hospital stay"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.1): "If the beneficiary is admitted to the SNF immediately following a 3-day qualifying hospital stay"

CLAIM: Hospital stay discharge counts as the day of leaving, and level of care at discharge is not determinative.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The beneficiary’s hospital discharge diagnoses included: chronic dementia, UTI, dehydration, myocardial infarction"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §100): "the level of care being furnished at that particular point is not a determining factor"

CLAIM: An assisted living resident may be confined to the home only if the facility is not primarily engaged in providing institutional medical care; this is not established.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "nursing services provided to Medicare beneficiary at his place of residence, an assisted living facility"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §30.1.2): "for purposes of Medicare coverage of home health services if he or she resides in an institution that is not primarily engaged in providing"

CLAIM: Services duplicative of what the facility must provide under State licensure are denied; the case facts do not say what the facility provides.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "nursing services provided to Medicare beneficiary at his place of residence, an assisted living facility"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §30.1.2): "would not be an optional substitute for the services that a facility is required to provide by law to its patients"

CLAIM: The qualifying 3-day inpatient stay requirement cannot be verified because the length of the GI bleeding hospital stay is not stated.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The beneficiary was re-admitted to * * * Health & Rehab Center (SNF) on December 11, 2008, following a hospital stay for gastrointestinal bleeding."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §10): "The beneficiary must have been an inpatient of a hospital for a medically necessary stay of at least 3 consecutive calendar days."

CLAIM: Disputed dates are after therapy discharge and the appellant does not contend care was unrelated to the terminal condition; hospice status is not stated.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The appellant does not contend that the SNF care at issue was unrelated to the beneficiary’s terminal condition."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.3.1): "Hospices contract with SNFs for services related to the beneficiary’s terminal condition."

CLAIM: The passages address venipuncture and catheters, not skilled nursing for insulin or medication management, and homebound status and plan of care are not stated.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "As the appellant acknowledges in its brief, the beneficiary tested blood sugar levels on her own."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.13): "The home health record must document the rationale for the blood draw as well as the results."

CLAIM: The hospital stay Feb 12 to Feb 17 counts as at least 3 consecutive days with the admission day counted and the discharge day not.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the beneficiary’s hospitalization from February 12 to February 17, 2010"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.1): "the day of admission, but not the day of discharge, is counted as a hospital inpatient day"

CLAIM: SNF care is needed for a condition treated in the hospital (hematuria), and SNF admission was at hospital discharge, within 30 days.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "At the time of discharge from the hospital on February 17 (for admission to the SNF)"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §10): "the beneficiary must require SNF care for a condition that was treated during the qualifying hospital stay"

CLAIM: SNF admission on the day of discharge from a 9-day inpatient stay meets the post-hospital and 30-day transfer requirements.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "first admitted to the SNF on August 25, 2011, following inpatient hospitalization from August 16, 2011, through August 25, 2011"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.2.1): "if initiated within 30 days after discharge from a hospital stay that included at least three consecutive days of medically necessary inpatient hospital services"

CLAIM: Skilled therapy is a covered type of service regardless of improvement potential, but SNF admission date and the qualifying stay timing are unclear in the case facts.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "demonstrates the clear need for the skills of a physical therapist"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4): "Coverage for such skilled therapy services does not turn on the presence or absence of a beneficiary’s potential for improvement"

CLAIM: Coverage requires an active written treatment plan after an initial evaluation in the SNF; this is not documented in the case facts.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The appellant also concedes that the beneficiary met her goals by September 11, 2008"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4.1.1): "The services must be directly and specifically related to an active written treatment plan"

CLAIM: Teaching safe transfers and stair use is a covered skilled PT type of service, but homebound status and a plan of care are not stated.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the skilled therapist was needed to teach the beneficiary how to safely transfer to and from the lift"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.2.2): "Physical therapy would be reasonable and necessary to teach the patient to climb and descend stairs safely."

CLAIM: Therapist visits solely to train home health aides are not billable, relevant to the D.W. maintenance-program goal.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "setting up a maintenance program for the home health aides to take over was a goal"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.2.1): "visits made by skilled therapists to a patient's home solely to train other HHA staff (e.g., home health aides) are not billable as visits"

CLAIM: Complications related to the urinary system requiring more frequent skilled care can be covered with documentation.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "He had a recurrence of urinary tract infection around mid-point during the six-month period at issue."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.7): "where there are complications that require more frequent skilled care related to the catheter, such care would, with adequate documentation, be covered"

CLAIM: Routine colostomy care is not skilled, but the beneficiary had a fistula and abscesses, indicating complications beyond routine care.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The beneficiary developed a fistula near the colostomy site."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §30): "changing the colostomy bag does not become a skilled nursing service when the nurse provides it"

CLAIM: Part-time or intermittent limits are 28 hours weekly, up to 35 case-by-case, but eligibility to receive home health at all is not shown.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "whether Medicare covered at least 28 hours and up to 35 hours of the home health services furnished to the beneficiary"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §50.7): "less than 8 hours each day and 28 or fewer hours each week"

CLAIM: Home health requires being confined to the home and a need for skilled nursing or therapy; case facts say nothing on these.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "coverage is available for home health aide or skilled nursing services on a part-time basis"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §30): "Be confined to the home"

CLAIM: Placement in a noncertified bed is addressed by the rule that payment is not made when the institution fails to place the patient in the appropriate bed.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "she was placed in a noncertified bed at the appellant’s facility"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §50): "or for any other reason the institution fails to place the patient in the appropriate bed"

CLAIM: The qualifying hospital stay condition appears met, but this does not cure the noncertified bed placement.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "both following a qualifying hospital stay"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §10): "stay of at least 3 consecutive calendar days"

CLAIM: IRF care is covered only if the patient meets specified requirements; the case facts contain no patient-level clinical information.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "This appeal involves IRF services provided by the appellant to five beneficiaries on various dates between March 2003 and May 2004."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §110): "IRF care is only considered by Medicare to be reasonable and necessary under 1862(a)(1)(A) of the Social Security Act"

CLAIM: SNF admission on July 27 followed an inpatient acute psychiatric stay beginning July 20, within 30 days of discharge.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "On July 27, 2009, the beneficiary was admitted to Twin Maples Health Care Facility, the appellant’s SNF."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.2.1): "if initiated within 30 days after discharge from a hospital stay that included at least three consecutive days of medically necessary inpatient hospital services"

CLAIM: Skilled observation and assessment can be covered for patients with psychiatric needs, as here.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the beneficiary was closely monitored by the skilled nurses (multiple times each day)"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.2.3.2): "Skilled observation and assessment may also be required for patients whose primary condition and needs are psychiatric in nature"

CLAIM: IRF coverage depends on meeting regulatory requirements; the case facts do not show all of them were met.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "Two days later, on July 17, 2003, the beneficiary was transferred and admitted to the appellant’s IRF"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §110): "IRF care is only considered by Medicare to be reasonable and necessary under 1862(a)(1)(A) of the Social Security Act"

CLAIM: A preadmission screening within 48 hours of IRF admission is required; none is described in the case facts.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "Upon admission, the beneficiary’s functional status was as follows: moderate assistance supine to sit, sit to stand"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §110.1.1): "a preadmission screening is an evaluation of the patient’s condition and need for rehabilitation therapy and medical treatment"

CLAIM: PT initiated for decreased strength with moderate assistance needed, but the passages require reasonable amount, frequency and duration, which the case does not settle

CASE FACT QUOTED: "At the beginning of PT, D.E. required moderate assistance for all functional transfers."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4.1.1): "this includes the requirement that the amount, frequency, and duration of the services must be reasonable"

CLAIM: A hospital stay of Dec 15-27, 2009 is asserted, which would exceed 3 consecutive days, but it is only the parties' contention

CASE FACT QUOTED: "December 15, 2009, through December 27, 2009, stay at"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §100): "some portion of the stay included at least 3 consecutive days of medically necessary inpatient hospital services"

CLAIM: Inpatient coverage depends on the medical record supporting the need for inpatient care; case facts do not show the clinical facts of the admissions

CASE FACT QUOTED: "Those cases that appear to be routine, expected discharge within 24 hours"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §10): "Admissions of particular patients are not covered or noncovered solely on the basis of the length of time the patient actually spends in the hospital."

CLAIM: Whether SNF level of care is met needs an individual determination; case facts give no case-mix classifier or skilled need beyond a plateau in PT

CASE FACT QUOTED: "after a qualifying hospital stay for treatment of delirium"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.1): "the beneficiary must receive an individual level of care determination using existing administrative criteria and procedures"

CLAIM: Nursing at an assisted living facility may be duplicative of facility-required services; case facts do not show the skilled need or facility obligations

CASE FACT QUOTED: "nursing services provided to Medicare beneficiary at his place of residence, an assisted living facility"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §30.1.2): "Medicare coverage would not be an optional substitute for the services that a facility is required to provide by law to its patients"

CLAIM: A qualifying 3-day hospital stay is required; the case does not state the length of the hospital stay

CASE FACT QUOTED: "following a hospital stay for gastrointestinal bleeding"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §10): "The beneficiary must have been an inpatient of a hospital for a medically necessary stay of at least 3 consecutive calendar days."

CLAIM: Skilled observation is reasonable until the treatment regimen has stabilized; nurses relayed fluctuating blood sugar logs and insulin was adjusted repeatedly

CASE FACT QUOTED: "sent logs evidencing fluctuating blood sugar levels to the beneficiary"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.1): "until the patient's clinical condition and/or treatment regimen has stabilized"

CLAIM: The hospital stay of Feb 12-17 meets the 3 consecutive day requirement

CASE FACT QUOTED: "hospitalization from February 12 to February 17, 2010, for"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §10): "The beneficiary must have been an inpatient of a hospital for a medically necessary stay of at least 3 consecutive calendar days."

CLAIM: SNF care is for hematuria, a condition treated in the qualifying hospital stay

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the beneficiary was diagnosed with hematuria secondary to prostate enlargement"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §10): "the beneficiary must require SNF care for a condition that was treated during the qualifying hospital stay"

CLAIM: SNF admission followed hospital discharge directly, within 30 days

CASE FACT QUOTED: "At the time of discharge from the hospital on February 17 (for admission to the SNF)"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.2.1): "initiated within 30 days after discharge from a hospital stay"

CLAIM: The 9-day hospitalization with direct SNF admission satisfies the post-hospital requirement, but skilled need after therapy discharge is not shown

CASE FACT QUOTED: "following inpatient hospitalization from August 16, 2011, through August 25, 2011, for"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.2.1): "initiated within 30 days after discharge from a hospital stay that included at least three consecutive days of medically necessary inpatient hospital services"

CLAIM: Coverage turns on need for skilled care, not improvement potential; the need for a therapist's skills is only asserted by the appellant

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The appellant also concedes that the beneficiary met her goals by September 11, 2008"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4): "Coverage for such skilled therapy services does not turn on the presence or absence of a beneficiary"

CLAIM: PT is not covered if expected results are insignificant relative to the therapy required

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The appellant also concedes that the beneficiary met her goals by September 11, 2008"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4.1.1): "Physical therapy services are not reasonable and necessary and would not be covered if the expected results are insignificant"

CLAIM: PT to teach safe stair or lift transfers can be reasonable and necessary, but is asserted by the appellant only

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The appellant further asserts that the skilled therapist was needed to teach the beneficiary how to safely transfer to and from the lift."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.2.2): "Physical therapy would be reasonable and necessary to teach the patient to climb and descend stairs safely."

CLAIM: Therapist visits solely to train HHA staff are not billable

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The appellant agreed that setting up a maintenance program for the home health aides to take over was a goal"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.2.1): "visits made by skilled therapists to a patient's home solely to train other HHA staff (e.g., home health aides) are not billable as visits"

CLAIM: Routine colostomy care without complications is not skilled, but this beneficiary developed complications near the colostomy site

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The beneficiary developed a fistula near the colostomy site."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §30): "A patient with a well-established colostomy absent complications may require assistance changing the colostomy bag"

CLAIM: Combined aide and nursing services under 8 hours a day and 28 hours a week (up to 35 case by case) are part-time; reasonableness of the hours is not shown

CASE FACT QUOTED: "whether Medicare covered at least 28 hours and up to 35 hours of the home health services"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §50.7): "less than 8 hours each day and 28 or fewer hours each week"

CLAIM: Both stays followed a qualifying hospital stay, presumed medically necessary

CASE FACT QUOTED: "both following a qualifying hospital stay."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.1): "Medical necessity will generally be presumed to exist."

CLAIM: Placement in a noncertified bed may still be paid under limitation of liability provisions; outcome not settled by the case facts

CASE FACT QUOTED: "she was placed in a noncertified bed at the appellant"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §50): "the services may be paid under certain conditions, based on the limitation of liability provisions"

CLAIM: IRF care is reasonable and necessary only if all 42 CFR 412.622 requirements are met; case facts give no clinical facts for the beneficiaries

CASE FACT QUOTED: "This appeal involves IRF services provided by the appellant to five beneficiaries"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §110): "IRF care is only considered by Medicare to be reasonable and necessary under 1862(a)(1)(A) of the Social Security Act if the patient meets all"

CLAIM: Skilled observation of psychiatric symptoms after a Haldol reduction, with potential to change treatment, was reasonable and necessary

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the psychiatrist reduced her Haldol from three to two times a day"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.2.3.2): "there is a reasonable potential that skilled observation and assessment by a licensed nurse will result in changes to the treatment of the patient"

CLAIM: Pneumonia treated with antibiotic and frequent nursing monitoring supports skilled observation

CASE FACT QUOTED: "and ongoing, frequent monitoring by the nursing staff"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.2.3.2): "there is a reasonable potential that skilled observation and assessment by a licensed nurse will result in changes to the treatment of the patient"

CLAIM: IRF stay requires all 412.622 requirements; case shows functional decline after knee replacement but not intensive therapy or other required elements

CASE FACT QUOTED: "Prior to the total knee replacement surgery, the beneficiary was independent with all of her activities of daily living"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §110): "IRF care is only considered by Medicare to be reasonable and necessary under 1862(a)(1)(A) of the Social Security Act if the patient meets all"

CLAIM: Medical record documents the patient's condition and need for therapy.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "D.E. was referred to PT due to decreased strength and decreased ADLs due to illness."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4.1.2): "Documentation of the patient’s condition in the medical record must describe the circumstances which delineate the need for skilled rather than"

CLAIM: Restorative therapy need is documented in the record.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "At the beginning of PT, D.E. required moderate assistance for all functional transfers."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4.1.1): "those services are reasonable and necessary and must be documented in the medical record"

CLAIM: Policy requires a qualifying 3-day medically necessary inpatient stay; hospital records are only said to be submitted by the provider.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The provider submits, as evidence of the three-day stay, hospital records concerning the beneficiary’s December 15, 2009, through December 27, 2009, stay"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §100): "at least 3 consecutive days of medically necessary inpatient hospital services"

CLAIM: Whether the hospital evidence is in the claim file is contested, so the record cannot be confirmed.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "that the relevant evidence regarding the qualifying three-day hospital stay was contained in the claim file"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.1): "coverage would be determined based on a review of the medical evidence in the file"

CLAIM: Admission order is required for inpatient coverage; case facts do not show whether it is in the record.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The medical record must contain information that documents the need for an inpatient level of care."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §10.2): "is therefore required for all hospital inpatient cases for hospital inpatient coverage and payment under Part A"

CLAIM: A 3-day qualifying hospital stay is required but the case facts contain no hospital or SNF records.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The appellant filed a timely request for Council review (Form DAB-101), dated August 24, 2009, and received on August 26, 2009."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20): "the individual must have been an inpatient of a hospital for a medically necessary stay of at least three consecutive calendar days"

CLAIM: Hospital stay is called qualifying but its inpatient length and dates are not given.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "after a qualifying hospital stay for treatment of delirium, a urinary tract infection (UTI), and dehydration"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §100): "at least 3 consecutive days of medically necessary inpatient hospital services"

CLAIM: Physician certification and supporting records are required, but none are described in the case facts.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The ALJ decisions concerned nursing services provided to Medicare beneficiary at his place of residence, an assisted living facility"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §30.5.1.2): "documentation in the certifying physician or allowed practitioner’s medical records"

CLAIM: The hospital stay before readmission has no stated length, so the 3-day requirement cannot be confirmed.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "following a hospital stay for gastrointestinal bleeding"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §10): "The beneficiary must have been an inpatient of a hospital for a medically necessary stay of at least 3 consecutive calendar days"

CLAIM: Skilled nursing need is documented in the visit records.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the records dated within this period include numerous documented instances of changes in the beneficiary’s medication schedule"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.7): "The need for the skilled services must be documented."

CLAIM: Nursing actions with documentation led to insulin changes.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the beneficiary’s insulin dosage was adjusted numerous times during this period"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.7): "such care would, with adequate documentation, be covered"

CLAIM: Inpatient stay of more than 3 days (admission day counted, discharge day not) is documented.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the beneficiary’s hospitalization from February 12 to February 17, 2010, for “worsening gross hematuria.”"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.1): "the day of admission, but not the day of discharge, is counted as a hospital inpatient day"

CLAIM: SNF care relates to a condition treated in the hospital and is documented by physician and nurses.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "As of March 2, 2010, a physician indicated that the beneficiary required skilled nursing for one week to monitor for signs of fever"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §10): "the beneficiary must require SNF care for a condition that was treated during the qualifying hospital stay"

CLAIM: SNF admission followed hospital discharge directly.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "At the time of discharge from the hospital on February 17 (for admission to the SNF)"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.2.1): "initiated within 30 days after discharge from a hospital stay"

CLAIM: Qualifying hospital stay and prompt SNF admission are documented.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "first admitted to the SNF on August 25, 2011, following inpatient hospitalization from August 16, 2011, through August 25, 2011"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.2.1): "initiated within 30 days after discharge from a hospital stay that included at least three consecutive days of medically necessary inpatient hospital services"

CLAIM: Therapy and nursing were furnished by the SNF after readmission.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "Following readmission, the beneficiary received physical therapy (PT), occupational therapy (OT), and nursing services."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §50.3): "must be provided by the SNF or by others under arrangements with the SNF"

CLAIM: Active written PT treatment plan based on an initial PT evaluation is required; only appellant assertions about documentation appear.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the documentation of record, present throughout all levels of review, demonstrates the clear need for the skills of a physical therapist"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4.1.1): "an active written treatment plan that is based upon an initial evaluation performed by a qualified physical therapist after admission to the SNF"

CLAIM: Therapist must document why a maintenance program was not developed earlier; only appellant assertions are given.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the therapist was “in the process of designing an appropriate home exercise program”"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.2.1): "When the development of a maintenance program could not be accomplished during the last visits(s) of rehabilitative/restorative treatment, the therapist must document why"

CLAIM: Patient and caregiver understanding must be documented; PT notes are cited but their content is not shown.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "at 133 (PT notes of February 7, 2006)"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.2.2): "The patient’s and caregiver’s understanding and implementation of the maintenance program must be documented."

CLAIM: Skilled need must be documented; the case facts describe conditions but not visit documentation.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The nurses noted abscesses in the rectum."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.7): "The need for the skilled services must be documented."

CLAIM: Routine colostomy care is not skilled; complications are noted but the nursing records are not described.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The beneficiary developed a fistula near the colostomy site."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §30): "changing the colostomy bag does not become a skilled nursing service when the nurse provides it"

CLAIM: Weekly and daily hour limits apply, but the actual hours of care furnished are not in the case facts.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "whether Medicare covered at least 28 hours and up to 35 hours of the home health services"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §50.7): "less than 8 hours each day and 28 or fewer hours each week"

CLAIM: Placement in a noncertified bed may be payable under limitation of liability, and the supporting evidence is not settled.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The beneficiary’s medical records indicate that she was placed in a noncertified bed at the appellant’s facility."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §50): "placed in a noncertified part of an institution which contains a participating “distinct part” SNF, the services may be paid under certain conditions"

CLAIM: IRF necessity requires an individual assessment of care needs; no IRF clinical records are described.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "This appeal involves IRF services provided by the appellant to five beneficiaries on various dates between March 2003 and May 2004."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §110): "based on an assessment of each beneficiary's individual care needs"

CLAIM: Psychiatric-related skilled observation must be carefully documented; monitoring by nurses and physicians is recorded.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the beneficiary was closely monitored by the skilled nurses (multiple times each day), one or more physicians"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.2.3.2): "Therefore, these cases must be carefully documented."

CLAIM: Hospital inpatient stay preceded SNF admission a week later.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the beneficiary (age 88) was admitted to the acute psychiatric unit at Yale University for dementia"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §10): "inpatient of a hospital for a medically necessary stay of at least 3 consecutive calendar days"

CLAIM: Preadmission screening documentation is required; the case facts do not say it exists, only prior function.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "Prior to the total knee replacement surgery, the beneficiary was independent with all of her activities of daily living"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §110.1.1): "the preadmission screening documentation must indicate the patient’s prior level of function"

CLAIM: Skilled therapy is supported by documented need for assistance with transfers.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "At the beginning of PT, D.E. required moderate assistance for all functional transfers."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4.1.1): "The services must be considered under accepted standards of medical practice to be specific and effective treatment"

CLAIM: A three-day prior hospital stay appears met for D.E. (medical necessity not shown, UNKNOWN).

CASE FACT QUOTED: "D.E. had a prior hospital stay for a diagnosis of congestive heart failure from August 23, 2009, to August 26, 2009."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.2.1): "at least three consecutive days of medically necessary inpatient hospital services"

CLAIM: PT assessment of strength and mobility after a hip fracture is skilled.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "J.M. was referred to PT secondary to a fall with fracture of the left hip with weakness."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4.1.2): "The skills of a physical therapist are required for the ongoing assessment of a patient"

CLAIM: The submitted hospital stay exceeds three inpatient days.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The provider submits, as evidence of the three-day stay, hospital records concerning the beneficiary"
